solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: London borough was the formal source of these rocks (7,6)

indicatorNotes.rocks: to rock something is to shake it back and forth, and shaken letters land in a new order

blocks.note: the first letter of 'these', where the word springs from

annotation.surface: A geologist claims a London district was the old, official origin of some particular stones.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rocks' looks like a noun, the stones the surface talks about; it is a verb telling you to shake up the letters. Waltham Forest is a borough in north-east London.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Waltham Forest is one of the 32 London boroughs.

entries.clue: Heat and rain to west vaguely given by meteorological device (7,7)

indicatorNotes.vaguely: something set out vaguely is not in its exact form, so the letters come in no fixed order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters; 'and' only joins the words

annotation.surface: A forecast of heat, and rain heading west, loosely produced by weather-measuring equipment.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a forecast, so the fodder hides in plain sight; drop 'and' and the remaining words give exactly fourteen letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: a weather station is a set of instruments that records temperature, rainfall and wind, so a meteorological device.

entries.clue: Something helping you forget Liberal American leader losing power (5)

indicatorNotes.losing: a leader losing power is left without P, so that letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: POTUS, President of the United States, minus its P

annotation.surface: A liberal US president who has lost his power is presented as something that helps you forget.
annotation.walkthrough: POTUS is the standard shorthand for the US president; P for power is a crossword convention.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary allusion: in the Odyssey, eating the lotus made Odysseus's men forget their homes.

entries.clue: A fight to interrupt reduction in unorthodoxy in this area (10)

indicatorNotes.to interrupt: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so A BOUT goes inside the other word
indicatorNotes.reduction: a reduction makes the word shorter, here by its last letter

blocks.note: HERESY = unorthodoxy, cut to HERES; first four letters
A + BOUT, a fight, as in boxing

annotation.surface: A scuffle breaks out in the middle of a cutback in heresy somewhere round here.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reduction in' reads as a decrease happening within unorthodoxy; it means the synonym itself is shortened, and the fight then splits it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: hereabouts means near here, in this area.

entries.clue: More than half of soccer team aboard vehicle upset left-winger (7)

indicatorNotes.aboard: someone aboard a vehicle is inside it, so SIX goes inside TRAM
indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, upset turns the column upside down, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: a tram is a vehicle; first letter

blocks.clueFragment: More than half of soccer team
blocks.note: a soccer team has eleven players, and six of them is more than half
rest of TRAM; the whole is then turned upside down

annotation.surface: Most of a soccer side, riding a bus, get upset by a left-wing player.
annotation.walkthrough: 'More than half of' tempts you to take letters from 'soccer team'; instead it is a number: six of the eleven players. Read T-SIX-RAM from the bottom up.
annotation.definitionFit: A Marxist is on the far political left; the surface's soccer team makes you read left-winger as a player on the left wing.

entries.clue: Limits to Universal blocking movie award regarding kissing (7)

indicatorNotes.Limits to: the limits of a word are its boundaries, its first and last letters
indicatorNotes.blocking: blocking something means standing in its way, so UL sits in the middle of the award

blocks.note: first and last letters of Universal

annotation.surface: Universal Pictures' boundaries stop an Oscar being awarded for kissing scenes.
annotation.walkthrough: Universal looks like the film studio, which suits the movie award; here only its first and last letters count.
annotation.definitionFit: A formal word: oscular comes from Latin osculum, a kiss, and means relating to kissing.

entries.clue: Boy with arrows climbed, bottom to top (4)

indicatorNotes.bottom to top: in a down clue the last letter is at the bottom, and it is carried up to the top

blocks.note: ROSE = climbed; its bottom letter moves to the top
the first three letters of ROSE, now below

annotation.surface: A boy carrying arrows scrambled up from the bottom to the top.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bottom to top' sounds like the boy climbing; it tells you to move only the bottom letter of the synonym up to the top.
annotation.definitionFit: A description by attribute: Eros, the Greek god of love, is pictured as a boy with a bow and arrows.

entries.clue: Fearful male stops growing substantially? (9)

indicatorNotes.stops: to stop a hole is to plug it, as a stopper does, so M plugs a gap inside the word

blocks.note: TREBLING, growing threefold; first three letters

annotation.surface: A frightened man stops growing much bigger.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stops' reads as ends; here it means plugs. The question mark admits that trebling is a stretched way to say growing substantially.
annotation.definitionFit: Trembling describes someone shaking with fear, so fearful.

entries.clue: A long time dismissing first English doctor in confused situation may be sign of pregnancy (9,5)

indicatorNotes.dismissing first: dismissing the first sends the opening letter away
indicatorNotes.in: things placed in a situation are inside it, so these pieces sit inside the synonym for confused situation

blocks.note: E = English, the first letter dismissed

annotation.surface: A long wait, a doctor dismissed and a muddle may all signal that someone is expecting.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is fair only with its 'may be': the dress is a sign of pregnancy because it is cut loose for a growing bump.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: wearing a maternity dress is one outward sign that a woman is pregnant.

entries.clue: Lot of surprise about leader in tournament table (5)

indicatorNotes.Lot of: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so the shortened word goes round the T

blocks.note: ALARM = surprise, cut to ALAR; first two letters

annotation.surface: Much of the shock surrounds whoever tops the league table.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tournament table' looks like a league table; 'table' alone is the definition, the one in a church.
annotation.definitionFit: A specific kind of table: the altar is the communion table in a church.

entries.clue: Stone work in The Wall, say (4,5)

blocks.note: an opera is a musical work (opus)

annotation.surface: Stonework built into a wall.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is masonry; The Wall is Pink Floyd's 1979 double album, and 'say' marks it as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Pink Floyd's The Wall is a well-known rock opera.

entries.clue: Chap’s instrument transferring current in Caribbean island (10)

indicatorNotes.transferring: transferring something moves it to a new place, so the I shifts to a new spot in the word

blocks.note: PIANOLA, a player piano, with I (current) moved from second place to after the N

annotation.surface: A man's musical instrument is shipped across to an island in the Caribbean.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like part of the transport story; it is I, the symbol for electric current.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Hispaniola is the Caribbean island shared by Haiti and the Dominican Republic.

entries.clue: Clever book penned by Porter? (4)

indicatorNotes.penned by: an animal penned is shut inside an enclosure, so B is shut inside the beer

blocks.note: porter is a dark beer, an ALE; first letter

annotation.surface: A smart book written by someone called Porter.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital P makes Porter look like an author; here it is the beer, and 'penned' means enclosed rather than written.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an able student is a capable, clever one.

entries.clue: Financial activity pre-empting any return from grasping nobleman (10)

indicatorNotes.grasping: to grasp is to hold tightly, so the tennis word holds the nobleman inside it

blocks.note: ACING: in tennis an ace is a serve the opponent cannot return; first two letters

annotation.surface: A money deal that heads off any comeback from a greedy aristocrat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Any return' suggests reversing a word; it is a tennis return, which an ace prevents.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: accounting, keeping and checking financial records, is a financial activity.

entries.clue: Eliminates our team, enthralling billions in big defeat (4,3)

indicatorNotes.enthralling: to enthral once meant to hold in bondage, so US holds B captive inside it
indicatorNotes.in: the pair sits in the defeat, inside its letters

blocks.note: a ROUT is a heavy defeat; first letter

annotation.surface: A sports report: our side is knocked out in a crushing defeat watched by billions.
annotation.walkthrough: Two layers nest here: billions inside our team, and that pair inside the defeat.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to rub out is to eliminate, whether erasing a mark or, in gangster slang, killing someone.

entries.clue: Difficulty about large fruit, one encountered for the first time? (5,4)

annotation.definition: one encountered for the first time?

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so the difficulty goes round the L

blocks.note: a BIND is a difficulty; first letter

annotation.surface: A problem with a big piece of fruit, one you had never met before.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: the person you meet on a blind date is someone encountered for the first time.
annotation.definitionFit: Blind date can mean the person as well as the outing, a partner you have never met before.

entries.clue: Disturbance in court sorted out (7)

indicatorNotes.sorted out: things sorted out are put in a new arrangement, and so are these letters

annotation.surface: A commotion in the courtroom is dealt with.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In court' reads as the scene of the fuss; it is the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, mostly British: a ruction is a noisy row or commotion.

entries.clue: Last of smoke swirling around secure kitchen appliance (4-3)

indicatorNotes.swirling: something swirling turns round, so the cigarette end reads backwards
indicatorNotes.around: around means enclosing, so the turned word goes round WIN

blocks.note: a butt is the last bit of a smoked cigarette; turned round, first letter

annotation.surface: The last wisps of smoke curl round a sealed appliance in the kitchen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Last of smoke' wants to be the letter E; it is a cigarette butt. A twin-tub is an old-style washing machine with separate wash and spin tubs.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a twin-tub washing machine often sat in British kitchens.

entries.clue: Drink provider, almost nude, is on Cheers (7)

indicatorNotes.almost: almost is nearly all, so the word stops one letter short

blocks.note: ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers

annotation.surface: A barman from the sitcom Cheers appears nearly naked.
annotation.walkthrough: Cheers looks like the TV show set in a bar, which suits a drink provider; here it simply means thanks.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: a barista makes and serves coffee.

entries.clue: Beset by anxiety about way of working (7)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so the anxiety goes round the way of working

blocks.note: MO = modus operandi, a way of working

annotation.surface: Someone is troubled by worries about how they do their job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beset by anxiety' reads as one phrase; the definition stops at 'Beset by', meaning surrounded by.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: to be amongst things is to be surrounded, beset, by them.

entries.clue: Want expert to contain agricultural disease, note (7)

indicatorNotes.to contain: to contain is to hold inside, so the expert holds the disease and note

blocks.note: an ACE is an expert; first letter

annotation.surface: We need a specialist to control an outbreak on the farm, please note.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Want' reads as a verb, to wish for; here it is the noun meaning lack.
annotation.definitionFit: An older sense: want as lack, as in 'for want of', is the absence of something.

entries.clue: Considerable time — one day? Years (4)

annotation.surface: A long stretch: a single day, or years?
annotation.walkthrough: Four abbreviations in a row. The definition uses the less familiar informal sense of tidy.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal sense: a tidy sum or tidy profit is a sizeable one.

entries.clue: Punishment area today finally covered in swirling raindrops (6,4)

indicatorNotes.covered in: something covered in a coat is inside it, so Y is wrapped inside the other letters
indicatorNotes.swirling: swirling things are whirled about, so the letters fall in a new order

annotation.surface: A penalty area is soaked by today's whirling rain at last.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Punishment area' hints at football's penalty area in the rain; it is where prisoners take their exercise.
annotation.definitionFit: A description by setting: a prison yard is the open space of a jail, where those being punished exercise.

entries.clue: Divert item required for the most part in A&E (5)

indicatorNotes.for the most part: the most part of a word is all but its end, so the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.in: placed in the hospital department means inside its letters

blocks.clueFragment: item required for the most part
blocks.note: a MUST is an essential item; without its last letter

annotation.surface: Redirecting a vital piece of kit that is needed in the emergency department.
annotation.walkthrough: A&E (Accident and Emergency) is the British hospital casualty department; only its two letters are used.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to divert people is to entertain them, as a diversion does.

entries.clue: Options to be selected from pieces supported by you (4)

indicatorNotes.supported by: in a down clue, a support sits underneath, so U goes beneath MEN

blocks.note: chess and draughts pieces are called men
U = you, as in text speak

annotation.surface: Choices to pick from among items you back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pieces' means chessmen or draughtsmen, not bits.
annotation.definitionFit: A description by function, whether a restaurant menu or a computer one: a list you choose from.

entries.clue: Radioactive element one’s lad found around Georgia (9)

indicatorNotes.found around: one thing found around another encloses it, so ONES wraps round GA

annotation.surface: A boy in Georgia turns out to be radioactive.
annotation.walkthrough: An obscure answer built from easy parts; oganesson is element 118, named after the physicist Yuri Oganessian.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: oganesson is a synthetic element that decays within milliseconds.

entries.clue: Some from The Sun irritated about being occupied (2,3)

indicatorNotes.Some from: some from a group is only part of it, so only part of the phrase's letters are taken
indicatorNotes.about: turned about means facing the other way, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: the last letter of The, all of Sun and the first of irritated, read right to left

annotation.surface: Some people from The Sun newspaper are annoyed at being kept busy.
annotation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid, which makes 'Some from' read like staff. Read thE SUN Irritated backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a phone or toilet that is in use is being occupied.

entries.clue: Visitors from university presumably having no time for reasonable supposition (8,5)

indicatorNotes.having no: visitors having no time are left without it, so the T is taken out

blocks.note: someone from a university is presumably educated

annotation.surface: Guests from a university take no time to reach a sensible conclusion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Visitors from university' reads as one group; 'from university presumably' describes them, and 'Visitors' alone is the word that loses a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: an educated guess is a supposition based on knowledge, so a reasonable one.
